model: Interactive Codex research collaboration, independent enumeration implementations

proposal.approach: Use Grassl’s construction for the upper bound and enumerate distance-compatible subspaces of every self-dual graph-state parent to exclude five.
proposal.derivation: The Grassl code attains six. Over every graph-state parent from the Danielsen–Parker classification including disconnected products, the distance-compatible rank-eight subspaces have no nonidentity stabilizers of weight at most five. Every eligible group extends to a graph-state parent up to weight-preserving equivalence.
proposal.what_would_change: A missing local-Clifford graph orbit, a distance-compatible parent plane with sufficiently many light stabilizers, or a logical of weight below four for the exhibited code would invalidate the certificate.

math_review.hypotheses: Binary stabilizer codes, no geometry assumptions. Every rank-eight isotropic subspace extends to a rank-ten graph-state parent up to a weight-preserving equivalence. All connected-component multisets are included. The independent Python graph6 decoder and census reproduced the C++ totals.
math_review.weakest_step: Low-weight errors of zero parent syndrome must be members of the selected subspace. Both implementations imposed this degeneracy condition and the missing-nonzero-syndrome condition. For all 47 embeddings among 3990 parent representatives the rank of nonidentity stabilizers of weight at most five was zero.

priority_review.comparison: The upper construction is Grassl’s. Zhang addressed lengths eleven and twelve using graph-state parents and excluded weight four at length ten. The reviewed primary sources did not explicitly resolve five versus six at length ten. This classification-assisted exclusion supplies the missing lower endpoint improvement, with the published graph-state classification as an external premise.
